content.title: About
content.content: Catfish fillet (NFS) is lean meat from freshwater catfish raised under the NFS (No Fish Stock) system. The fish has a mild flavor, firm texture, and high protein content, making it popular in many cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Catfish can grow over a meter long, but food‑grade fish are usually harvested at 2–3 kg.
The NFS system uses feeds that do not contain wild‑caught fish, reducing pressure on marine ecosystems.
Catfish meat is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids but contains less fat than salmon.
Catfish can breathe air, allowing cultivation in low‑oxygen water conditions.
In some cultures catfish is considered a delicacy and served as steaks, kebabs, or fried pieces.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Catfish fillet provides about 18–20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Its lean profile fits calorie‑controlled diets and helps maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Contains EPA and DHA, which are beneficial for heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides phosphorus, selenium, and potassium, supporting bone and nervous system health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to catfish.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Fish raised in polluted waters can accumulate mercury or cadmium; choose products from reputable sources.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage or insufficient cooking can allow bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Catfish fillet can be baked, grilled, steamed, or braised. Before cooking, rinse and pat dry; optionally marinate in lemon juice, olive oil, and herbs. Cooking time varies with thickness, typically 8–12 minutes over medium heat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fillets in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C in an airtight container for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where quality is maintained for up to 3 months. Discard any fillet with an off‑odor.

content.title: About
content.content: Whiting (Merlangius merlangus) is a marine fish from the cod family that inhabits the coastal waters of the Atlantic Ocean and the North Sea. Grilled whiting has delicate white flesh, a mildly sweet flavor, and a crisp crust when cooked over a grill or pan.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whiting can grow up to 80 cm and weigh more than 5 kg, but it is usually sold as fillets weighing 150–250 g.
In Europe, whiting is a traditional dish in North Sea countries, often prepared over an open flame.
The fish is high in protein and virtually carbohydrate‑free, making it popular among athletes and weight‑watchers.
Whiting can change the colour of its skin to blend with its surroundings, helping it avoid predators.
The skin, when grilled, becomes crispy and adds a pleasant aroma to the dish.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving of grilled whiting provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other fish, whiting contains very little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Whiting is a good source of vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The fish supplies selenium, iodine and phosphorus, important for thyroid health and bone strength.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower in omega‑3 than fatty fish, whiting still contributes to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Whiting can accumulate trace amounts of mercury and other heavy metals; moderate consumption is advised, especially for children and pregnant women.

items.title: Over‑cooking
items.content: Excessive grilling can produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Whiting is usually prepared whole or as fillets, seasoned with salt, pepper and a drizzle of olive oil, then grilled or pan‑seared until golden. Serve with lemon wedges, fresh herbs, vegetable sides, or a light yogurt‑based sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh whiting should be kept in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C, wrapped in plastic, and used within 2 days. Frozen fish can be stored at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen fillets in the fridge; discard any fish with an off‑odor.

content.title: About
content.content: Milk 'n Cereal Bar is a ready‑to‑eat snack consisting of whole grain cereal, dried fruit, nuts and a milk‑yogurt coating. Each bar weighs 30 g, provides 150 kcal, 5 g protein, 20 g carbohydrates and 5 g fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Designed as a quick breakfast or energy snack for active people.
Contains whole rolled oats that retain most of their fiber.
The milk layer includes probiotic cultures that support gut health.
No artificial colors or flavors are added.
Packaging is made from recyclable material and is fully recyclable.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Whole oats are rich in soluble fiber, which helps maintain normal digestive function.

items.title: Contains probiotics
items.content: The yogurt coating provides live Lactobacillus cultures that promote a balanced microbiome.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Includes thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: Sweetness comes from dried fruit; added sugar is limited to 5 g per serving.

items.title: Supports muscle maintenance
items.content: 5 g of plant protein help replenish amino acid stores after workouts.

items.title: Nut and dairy allergy
items.content: The bar contains nuts and a dairy yogurt coating, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Rolled oats may contain trace gluten, important for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density for strict diets
items.content: 150 kcal per bar can be significant on very low‑calorie diets, so consider overall daily intake.

items.title: Sugar content for diabetics
items.content: Although modest, the sugar amount should be monitored by people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar is ready to eat straight from the wrapper. It’s convenient to take to the gym, on a trip, or to work. For a more filling breakfast, you can slice it and add to yogurt or kefir.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bars in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, consume within 7 days. For longer storage, keep in an airtight container.

pasta-whole-grain-with-tomato-based-sauc.title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce and Meat

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with tomato sauce and meat is an Italian dish made from whole‑grain pasta, a rich tomato‑based sauce, and tender pieces of stewed meat. The whole‑grain pasta retains bran and germ, making it more nutritious than regular refined pasta.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta provides more fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals than traditional white pasta.
Tomato sauce is a good source of lycopene, an antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
Traditionally the meat in the sauce is beef or pork, sometimes enriched with Italian salami.
The dish is often finished with grated Parmesan and fresh basil.
In restaurant 3646 it is a signature item that consistently receives high guest ratings.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta supports healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes supply lycopene, which may reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Complete protein from meat
items.content: Meat provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the whole grain pasta and meat are sources of B1, B3, and B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish contains iron, zinc, and magnesium, important for immune function and muscle health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten, so it should be avoided by people with celiac disease.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce often includes added salt; individuals with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Meat fat content
items.content: Using fatty cuts can make the dish calorie‑dense; leaner cuts are a healthier choice.

items.title: Acidity of tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes may trigger heartburn in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, tossed with the sauce and meat. Top with grated cheese, fresh basil, or a drizzle of olive oil for extra flavor. Optional additions include vegetables such as broccoli, spinach, or zucchini.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze up to 1 month after cooling to room temperature.

content.title: About
content.content: A low‑calorie sports drink is designed to replenish water and electrolytes after intense exercise while providing minimal calories. It is enriched with electrolytes (sodium, potassium, magnesium) and B‑vitamins, and flavored with natural extracts without added sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Low‑calorie sports drinks often use sweeteners like stevia or sucralose instead of sugar.
Electrolytes help prevent cramps and speed up muscle recovery.
B‑vitamins aid in converting carbohydrates into energy more efficiently.
Some versions contain creatine or beta‑alanine for extra endurance support.
Low‑calorie formulas usually have a lighter texture and are absorbed faster.

items.title: Electrolyte balance restoration
items.content: Sodium, potassium and magnesium replace losses from sweating and support normal muscle function.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: B‑vitamins (B6, B12, niacin) participate in carbohydrate metabolism, helping maintain energy levels without extra calories.

items.title: Reduced dehydration risk
items.content: Electrolyte‑enhanced hydration is more effective than plain water during long, intense workouts.

items.title: Muscle recovery aid
items.content: Some formulas include branched‑chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine) that promote protein synthesis and faster recovery.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: Ideal for those monitoring energy intake while still needing workout support.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Flavorings, sweeteners or added additives may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Excess electrolyte intake
items.content: High sodium levels can be problematic for people with hypertension or kidney disease.

items.title: Sweetener sensitivity
items.content: Artificial sweeteners may cause gastrointestinal discomfort for some users.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Elevated potassium can affect the action of certain drugs, such as diuretics.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix one serving (usually 30 g) with 250–300 ml of water, stir until fully dissolved, and drink immediately after training or during prolonged activity. Do not exceed the recommended daily amount.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the package tightly sealed to prevent moisture. Follow the expiration date printed on the packaging.

taco-flour-tortilla-with-beans-cheese.title: Flour Tortilla with Beans and Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A flour tortilla filled with beans and cheese is a classic Mexican snack consisting of a soft wheat‑based flatbread stuffed with cooked beans and melted cheese. The combination provides carbohydrates, plant protein, and dairy fat for a balanced source of energy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flour tortillas originated in northern Mexico in the 19th century as a wheat alternative to corn tortillas.
Beans are one of the oldest cultivated legumes, grown for more than 7,000 years.
Cheese in Mexican cuisine is often a meltable cheddar‑style or “queso” that softens quickly.
Tortillas are conveniently folded into tacos, making them a popular street‑food item.
The bean‑cheese combo provides a complete set of essential amino acids.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Beans deliver about 8 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber in beans aids digestion and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Provides calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Cheese adds calcium for bone health and phosphorus for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Beans are high in thiamine and folate, which support the nervous system and metabolism.

items.title: Energy‑dense
items.content: The tortilla supplies quick‑release carbs, making it a good pre‑activity fuel.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to the cheese component.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheeses often contain salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Gluten in wheat tortilla
items.content: Those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: Beans can cause gas
items.content: Legumes may lead to bloating for some; soaking beans before cooking can reduce this effect.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Warm the tortilla on a skillet or microwave, add hot beans, sprinkle shredded cheese and fold. Optional toppings include fresh vegetables, salsa, or guacamole for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep tortillas in an airtight bag in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Store the prepared bean‑cheese filling separately in a container and use within 3‑4 days. Freeze extra tortillas for up to 2 months.
